topics.title: Programming Fundamentals
topics.summary: Programming is creating instructions for computers. Every program follows 3 stages: Input (information entered), Process (computer follows steps), and Output (results displayed).
topics.example_code:
# Input -> Process -> Output
# Displaying an instruction:
print("Step 1: Plant seed")

topics.title: What is Python?
topics.summary: Python executes instructions sequentially from top to bottom. Python is case-sensitive: always use lowercase print().
topics.example_code:
print("Prepare the soil")
print("Plant the seeds")
print("Water the garden")

topics.title: Comments
topics.summary: Text after # is ignored by Python during execution. Use comments to leave notes and explain your code to humans.
topics.example_code:
# This line is a note for programmers
water = 5  # Inline comment
print("Notes are free")

topics.title: print() Function
topics.summary: print() shows text or values in the console. Text goes inside quotes. Several values can be separated with commas.

topics.title: Variables
topics.summary: A variable stores a value under a name using =. You can access and update variables. Names cannot begin with numbers or have spaces.

topics.title: Strings & Concatenation
topics.summary: Strings represent text in quotes. Combine them using + (concatenation). Measure the number of characters in a string with len().

topics.title: Math Operators
topics.summary: Use + - * / for arithmetic. // divides and drops decimals (floor division), % gives remainder (modulus), ** is exponentiation.

topics.title: if and else
topics.summary: if runs code only when a condition is true. else runs when it is not. Indent the code inside by 4 spaces.

topics.title: for loops and range()
topics.summary: A for loop repeats code. range(3) gives 0, 1, and 2, so the loop body runs three times. Use i + 1 to start display numbers at 1.
topics.example_code:
for i in range(3):
    print("Water plant", i + 1)

topics.title: Lists and Indexing
topics.summary: Lists store multiple items in order inside square brackets []. Python uses zero-based indexing: the first item is at index [0].
topics.example_code:
basket = ["Rose", "Mint", "Fern"]
print(basket[0])  # Rose
print(basket[1])  # Mint
basket.append("Sunflower")
